description:
(Summary from jobright.ai; the original posting may say more.)

Intelligence Security Laboratories is hiring an Infrastructure Engineer to build and maintain the IT and network infrastructure that supports its growth. The role designs, deploys, secures, and maintains networks, services, and workstations in a security-sensitive environment.
Infrastructure Engineer designing secure LAN/VPN networks, deploying containerized services, configuring workstations, and maintaining high-availability recovery systems

Responsibilities:
• Plan, design, and deploy complex networks including custom LAN and VPN configurations
• Deploy and monitor various services to be used by employees and associates. (requires intimate knowledge of containerization)
• Build custom operating system and workstation configurations within the network to ensure practical security while maintaining efficient workflows
• Ensure high availability by maintaining backup systems and recovery procedures
• Generate and maintain accurate documentation of all systems and configurations
• Provide support for connectivity and availability problems
• Collaborate with developers, infrastructure engineers, and other non-technical team members to support a high efficiency, secure workflow

Requirements:
• At least 4 years of personal or professional Linux systems administration experience
• A relevant bachelors degree
• Deep understanding of computer network concepts:
  + TCP/IP, LAN/WAN, DNS, VPN, SSL/TLS, Routing, DHCP, OSI model, Firewalls
• Hands-on experience with containerization/virtualization platforms
• Understanding of the Linux operating system:
  + How kernel modules, filesystems, networking work, etc
• Linux system administration experience
  + Scripting, user management, networking

Preferred:
• CI/CD Infrastructure experience
• LXC, Docker, Podman
• Libvirt, Proxmox (or any virtualization platform)
• Administering small, custom, or airgapped networks
• Homelab experience
• Cybersecurity competitions (CCDC, CPTC, CyberForce, CTF, etc...)
• Experience in custom or highly-regulated IT environments such as HIPAA, FERPA, FedRAMP, IL6, or JWICS
• Current or past U.S. government security clearance
